en: Before dying and departing this world,
Or shall I leave it merely a khan?
For measured life, death is certain;
For those with lungs, inflammation is real.
God is one, the Quran is true.
They said a hero does not die without an heir;
I am passing without an heir.
They said a hero does not die without a child;
I am passing without a child.
Think again, uncle:
If, spear in hand, I break the ranks,
And my allotted water runs out,
My destined end comes and a bullet takes me,
If Allah ordains this,
I have no choice but to bear it.
My poor wife does not give birth;
I have no son to leave behind.
My horses in the mountains number ninety thousand;
The fleet tulpars have no brains.
One day I shall leave the world;
My treasury has no master to tend it!'
Grieving, weeping, distraught,
Kanykei sobbed bitterly.
She too implored the one God;
As she stood weeping for a child,
The wretched husband and wife,
As they made such a prayer,
Birches wept, willows wept;
Every soul who watched them wept.
Facing the qibla,
The panther Koshoy, blessed by Khizyr,
Spread his hands and said, 'Amen.'
Then he raised his hands.
Koshoy gave his blessing;
Infidels and Muslims
Gave their blessing together.
You were a child conceived through that blessing,
To Temir Khan's city
You came, a wandering soul.
You beat a bald man in the forest;
Your father was so great a lion,
Yet you hemmed me in on every side.
Loaded upon sixty camels,
You have no caravan migrated from the Argyn.
Kongurbay slaughtered your father;
You have no mother's vengeance against me.
This forest of mine is no open plain.
Your mother's breasts—
Those who struck them open and drove her away,
Abyke and Köbösh in Talas, are not me.
A drop flowing down from Alai—
There is a mark upon her fatty rump.
Upon your bereaved mother's flesh
Is the mark of that wretch Abyke's whip.
Spurring when there is no wind,
Is there a wretch like you?
Calling his own mother his elder sister—
Is there a wretch like you?'
His lineage from generation to generation,
Sary Taz told him insistently.
All the hidden particulars,
Sary Taz dug out and told.
All that had passed and gone,
His fathers and forefathers,
Sary Taz told, leaving none out.
His lineage from generation to generation,
Sary Taz told, leaving none out.
Hearing the bald charcoal-burner's words,
Learning that his people were different,
That Talas was his land,
That the Kyrgyz were his people,
He heard the tale without delay:
That mighty Manas, gone to the Last Judgment,
Was his father.
Hearing this, he was distraught;
His tears streamed in every direction.
He pleaded with Sary Taz:
'My dear Uncle Sary,
Not knowing, I treated you like a dog.
If I do not know, tell me again;
Let me obey what you say.
My hand struck you, Uncle Sary.
My mother Kanykei—
I will give her to you as a gift.
Take my words without resentment;
Take my mother and bear no grudge.
Leave the two of mine, take one of mine;
Take my words without resentment;
Take out my eye without hurting me!
Not knowing, I struck you.
Aktulpar is for sale, I am a gift.
My dear khan and uncle,
Uncle Sary who lives in the forest,
If your resentment grows too great,
Take my horse, the splendid Aktulpar;
I will lie down before you—
Take my life as I cry out!'
Semetey asked again;
Again the same tale was told;
Sary Taz told it again,
Again, just as before.
He asked again, yet again;
He told it again, yet again,
The same tale once more.
'My dear Uncle Sary,
You made me know what I did not know;
What learned man could compare with you!
You made me understand what I could not grasp;
My very life is a sacrifice to you.
Give me your hand, uncle;
I will show your eyes
A marvel no one has seen!
If these words of yours are true,
If what you say is right and exact,
If Khan Manas, gone to the other world,
Is truly my father,
If my father, Khan Manas,
Was indeed a lord,
If poor Elder Sister Kanykei
Is truly my mother,
Your charcoal is no charcoal, but an offering;
This kindness you have done
Shall bear witness for you.
If God lets me see Talas,
Among the Argyn and Kyrgyz,
If I take my place as ruler,
I will send word to my people.
Making you my own protector,
Making you sovereign over my people,
If I reach my land alive,
At least over the Argyn
I will raise you as khan.
Moving you out of this forest,
Erasing the name of Sary Taz,
I will cut away your misfortune.
If I do not die young,
I will name you Sary Khan!
Give me your hand, uncle;
I will open your path for all to see.
I will surely wash away
The misery filling your brow.
If these words of yours are false,
That single eye in your forehead—
I will gouge out your one eye;
Beside your charcoal,
I will slaughter you as a sacrifice!'
Clasping his hand and speaking,
Making his promise firm,
Taking the falcon by its jesses,
Striking the tulpar on the neck,
He turned back and rushed away.
Darkening into gloom,
He galloped toward Bukhara.
Hearing the bald man's words in the wilds,
Learning his lineage was Kyrgyz,
Hearing the strange bald man's words,
Learning his father was another,
Hearing the bald charcoal-burner's words,
Learning his father was Manas,
'Your horse has a blaze,' he was told,
'Your father is another,' he was told.
Aychürök was his relation through marriage,
The luckless one he would wed,
The daughter of a fairy, his wife.
Kanykei in Bukhara,
Whom he called his sister, was his mother,
The brow upon his forehead,
The Mecca above his head.
Once he knew she was his mother,
And Manas, gone to the other world,
Once he knew he was his father,
His father had departed this world—
He learned that he had died.
His dear mother Kanykei,
Fleeing, wandering to Bukhara—
He learned that she had come there.
Having just heard the bald man's words,
Learning his father was Manas,
He offered a prayer to Baabedin;
To the one Almighty Allah
He vowed a horse with crescent hooves.
The boy hurried, distraught;
The noble falcon gone to the other world,
Once he knew him as his father,
His heart burst with joy.
Without a speck upon his eyelashes,
His fortune opened like the sun,
At that moment, the boy's
Every sorrow scattered.
Raging against Bukhara,
Traveling toward Bukhara city,
Good fortune to him—he took offense
At Bukhara's Khan Temir.
Offended with Bukhara city,
Semetey was resolved to resent
The whole of Bukhara.
A prince's child—
Could it be right to keep him hidden?
Falsely calling him 'my son,'
Ismayyl had been telling lies.
Could there ever be two?
The offspring of a noble lord—
Could it be right for him to wander?
The sole child of a khan of noble stock,
Temir Khan had kept him;
Could this khan ever prosper?
Semetey grew furious;
With a shout he rode toward Bukhara.
Sparing no horseflesh, he traveled far;
Coming onto the plain, he shouted.
The hapless orphan of surpassing fortune,
As he reached one place or another,
Raised the battle cry, 'Manas!'
'Talas, Talas, Talas!' he cried,
Repeating the name of the land.
'Generous Sultan Manas!' he cried,
Repeating the hero's name.
The earth seemed to split as he sped along;
The accomplished Semetey
Drew near to Bukhara.
On the day he would enter Bukhara,
Temir Khan harbored malice:
'If he meets him in the forest,
He will return in a fury.
Every seditious word,
That pig Sary Taz will tell him.
Hearing that bastard bald man's words,
Learning his homeland is elsewhere,
The boy will come back in a fury.
This Bukhara standing here,
He will destroy it before leaving.
He will plunder its riches.
Believing those seditious words,
He will wreak terrible disorder!
Whatever happens, Semetey,
The offspring of an unyielding hero,
Will wreck my treasury and depart.
He will cut off the khans' heads;
He will put an end to me along with them!'
In his fear, Temir Khan,
Through Sary Taz's enmity,
Became an enemy to his own kin.
Bukhara's khan, Temir Khan,
Had been corrupt from the outset.
In alarm, he began to speak,
Speaking quietly, laying his words down firmly.
To the court of broad Bukhara,
Its wise men and elders,
Temir Khan had gathered them,
All who could devise a plan,
Its quick and fluent speakers.
Gathering many of them,
They set the matter before the gathering,
But could find no counsel.
They set their words before the gathering,
But could find no way out.
